question: Would the study's reader give a published level with only a scrap of uncited lines left?
note: Round 1's control blanked every line the reading cites on any question, and two of its three levels held: the reader was not shown to move at all. Here the control blanks every line but a remnant: for each cited block, one uncited block of the same size, drawn with the published evaluation's hash as the seed. No line any reading cites is left; the seed, the rubric and the reading prompt stay whole, and each source keeps its name, format and line count. A blank world would test nothing here, because the study's reader cites a non-blank line for every level and could give none. It is a floor: a move shows the reader reads the world, not that it tells worlds apart at the published grain. Round 1 repeated each baseline already, so this round leaves the repeat out to stay at 27 calls, and its standing is not stable.

frames.name: fable-5-1-recognition
frames.receives: The study's working record, beside round 1's verdict on the same decision and the Study page's note on how close the levels sit.

predictions.reason: Round 1 read 3 in all six baseline and repeat sessions and in all three ablated ones. The remnant is 92 lines, most of them tests and a few lines of the apparatus, with none of the world's account of itself, so too little of the poem's tension is there to read at 3; the control falls and the reader can tell.
predictions.otherwise: Unresolved, the reader cannot tell, if the remnant holds at 3: the level would come from the seed and the question, or from what any scrap of a careful world shows, rather than from this world as read. Unresolved with no agreed level, if the remnant splits.
